summary: Iran talks in Oman as tankers burn near Hormuz, Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge, Israel's Knesset picks a speaker, COP31 drafts a deal, and AI faces a big test week.

question.text: Russia says it shot down 1,336 drones in one night and calls the Crimean Bridge damage minor; the IRGC says it hit a US radar that Bahrain says was never touched. When only one side can count, what would convince you a number is true?

read.title: Five Features of APEC to Know About With Trump, Putin, and Xi Set to Attend
read.summary: A short guide to this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen: who the 21 members are, who is coming, and the issues from Hormuz to Taiwan and trade that could shape it.

topics.heading: Iran's foreign minister holds talks in Oman as more tankers are hit near Hormuz
topics.summary: Abbas Araghchi met Oman's foreign minister in Muscat, who called the talks "constructive", while tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz and the IRGC claimed a third drone attack on a US radar in Bahrain.[^2][^3][^4] US Vice President JD Vance said Trump will not let the war become a "forever war".[^1]

lead.title: Vance says Trump will avoid 'forever war' in Iran

alsoReported.title: Middle East conflict: Tanker incident near Hormuz as Vance rules out 'forever war'
Live Updates: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims another attack on U.S. radar system in Bahrain

article: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Muscat early Tuesday and met Oman's foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi.[^2] Albusaidi wrote on X that it was "a constructive meeting" and that the two discussed current diplomatic efforts and the need for "de-escalation and peaceful solutions".[^3] Oman has long carried messages between Tehran and Washington. The day before, the Trump administration called Iran's seven conditions for a deal "unacceptable", according to CBS News.[^4]

The fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane that carries much of the Gulf's oil, continued. The UK's maritime security agency (UKMTO) said a tanker about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, was attacked on Monday evening and set on fire, and that a second strike hit it on Tuesday.[^2] Iran's navy said one tanker had hit a mine, while UKMTO described an "unknown projectile".[^4] India's ports minister said all 24 Indian sailors aboard another hit tanker, the Tara Gas, were safe.[^2]

On Tuesday morning the Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said their drones attacked a US-run radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, their third such claim since Friday. Bahrain's state TV said the attack was thwarted.[^2][^4] Iran also says inspectors from the UN nuclear watchdog will not get into its main nuclear sites until "the war has permanently ended".[^4]

In Washington, Vance told Fox News that the US will not let the conflict become "a 10- or 15-year commitment, or frankly even a two-year commitment", but he gave no end date.[^1] Oil fell slightly on Monday, with Brent at about $95 a barrel, still well above the roughly $72 it cost before the war began in late February.[^4]

My read: Tuesday shows two tracks running at once, quiet diplomacy through Oman and steady pressure at sea. Xi Jinping hosts Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on Nov 19, and China's Middle East envoy has just visited Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia, so the next signal may come from there.[^1]
topics.differences: Accounts of the tanker attacks differ: Iran's navy blames sea mines, UKMTO reported an unknown projectile, and Gulf News described a missile attack on the Tara Gas.[^2][^4] The IRGC says its drones hit a US radar in Bahrain; Bahrain says it stopped the attack.[^2][^4]

topics.heading: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge during what Russia calls the war's biggest drone attack
topics.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea on Monday. Russia says it downed 1,336 drones overnight, a record, and calls the bridge damage minor; footage suggests visible damage to one span.[^6][^7] Russian strikes left over 52,000 households in Odesa region without power.[^8]

lead.title: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge in record drone attack

alsoReported.title: Ukraine Hits Crimean Bridge Amid Record Overnight Drone Attack
Russia's Prized Kerch Bridge Struck In Ukrainian Drone Onslaught

article: Early on Monday, Ukrainian drones hit the Crimean Bridge, also called the Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia to the Crimean peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014.[^5][^7] Crimea's Russian-installed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, restricted road traffic until at least midday, and rail traffic resumed later that morning.[^5][^6] Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the damage "minor".[^6]

Not everyone agrees. The War Zone, a US defence site, said Russian state TV footage showed a deformed road span and that satellite images showed damage near one arch, though the full extent was unclear.[^7] It also reported that about 2,000 vehicles were stuck in queues before the bridge reopened in one direction.[^7] The bridge matters because it is a key supply route for Russian forces in southern Ukraine; Ukraine has struck it several times since a truck bomb in October 2022.[^5]

Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 1,336 drones overnight, the most of the war, and 2,049 over 24 hours, including some cruise missiles. These figures could not be independently checked.[^7] Moscow's mayor said about 600 drones flew toward the capital.[^6] Ukraine says it hit the Ilsky oil refinery in southern Russia, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine has disabled over 55% of Russia's refining capacity, a claim Bloomberg could not verify.[^8]

Russia kept hitting Ukraine's power system too. Strikes on energy sites in Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia and Cherkasy killed at least two people, and more than 52,000 households in Odesa region lost power, local officials and the energy company DTEK said.[^8]

Peace talks in Abu Dhabi last week brought no real progress.[^8] A Kremlin aide says a Putin-Trump meeting is being arranged and that ending the war is among the agreed topics, while US officials say Ukraine is not expected to feature in the three-way meeting with Xi on Nov 19.[^7][^8]
topics.differences: Russia calls the bridge damage minor; The War Zone points to footage and satellite images showing a deformed span.[^6][^7] Drone totals come only from Russia's defence ministry and are unverified.[^7] On the Nov 19 summit, the Kremlin says Ukraine is on the agenda for a Putin-Trump meeting; US officials say the war is not expected to come up in the three-way talks.[^7][^8]

topics.heading: Israel's Knesset votes on a new speaker in the first test of Eisenkot's bloc
topics.summary: Gadi Eisenkot's bloc, backed by Arab-led parties, wants to replace a Netanyahu ally as Knesset speaker with Matan Kahana in a vote set for Tuesday evening.[^9] Its allies fear Likud may delay the vote with a long speech.[^10]

lead.title: As Knesset readies for new speaker, Israeli opposition holds powerful role

alsoReported.title: Knesset speaker vote at risk of delays as Eisenkot bloc fears Likud-backed filibuster

article: Israel's new parliament, the 26th Knesset, was sworn in on Nov 10 after an election that went against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp.[^9] Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister while coalition talks continue. On Tuesday, members vote on a new speaker, and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc has nominated Matan Kahana of his Yashar party.[^9]

The speaker sounds like a procedural job, but it carries real power: the speaker sets parliament's agenda, runs debates and can call a confidence vote on the government.[^9] Arab-led parties have said they will back Kahana. Joint List leader Ahmad Tibi told Al Jazeera they want to remove "the Netanyahu coalition as soon as possible".[^9]

Procedure could slow things down. The Jerusalem Post, citing Israel's N12 News, reports that Eisenkot's camp fears a Likud minister could speak for hours to push the vote late into the night.[^10] Debate was due to start at 4 p.m. with a vote expected around 8 p.m.; Likud officials called Yashar's plan to limit speeches "a heavy-handed measure".[^10]

If Kahana wins, the opposition plans bills to set up an independent inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attack, restore the attorney general's powers, undo changes that weakened the courts, and limit prime ministers to two terms, which would rule out Netanyahu.[^9] My read: a win would show Eisenkot can command a majority even before he forms a government, which may change how Likud approaches unity talks.
topics.differences: Eisenkot's camp says the speaker vote is an internal matter of parliament that does not justify unlimited speeches; Likud officials say limiting debate is heavy-handed.[^10]

topics.heading: COP31's first draft deal leaves fossil fuels and climate finance wide open
topics.summary: Negotiators in Antalya released an 18-page draft text with two options on fossil fuels, "transitioning away" or "phase out", and open fights over finance and a 35% electricity target.[^11] Ministers now take over, with talks due to end Friday.[^12]

lead.title: First draft of COP31 deal signals tough negotiations to come

alsoReported.title: COP31 turns to ministers for deal on finance, energy

article: The UN climate summit COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, entered its final week on Monday with a first draft of the final deal.[^11] Talks began on Nov 9 with almost 200 countries. Turkey hosts and Australia leads the negotiations under a shared arrangement agreed after a dispute over hosting.[^12]

The 18-page draft gives two choices on fossil fuels: repeating the 2023 promise of "transitioning away" from them, or a stronger call to "phase out" coal, oil and gas. Both could be dropped from the final text.[^11] It also marks disagreement over Turkey's proposal that electricity should provide 35% of the world's energy use by 2035, up from about 20% now, and over how much rich countries should pay to help poorer ones adapt to climate change.[^11][^12]

The splits are familiar. The Arab Group said it will not accept global targets imposed from above or targets for specific sectors or energy sources, while the EU, Pacific island states and the least developed countries backed the presidency's approach.[^12] Australian minister Chris Bowen, who leads the talks, said the final deal will not look exactly like the draft but that it is right for it to discuss fossil fuels.[^11] An analyst at the think tank E3G said the approach looks like putting everything in and letting countries fight over the trade-offs.[^11]

Why it matters: a UN report last month said the world is on track to pass 1.5C of warming, the limit set in the Paris Agreement.[^11] COP decisions need consensus, so one bloc can block wording. My read: expect the fossil fuel language to be the last thing settled, and the talks may run past Friday, as UN climate summits often do.[^11]
topics.differences: Oil-producing Arab states reject global or sector-specific targets; the EU, Pacific island states and the poorest countries support the presidency's push for stronger outcomes.[^12]

topics.heading: Nvidia reports without its founder as Anthropic prices its IPO and US tightens chip rules
topics.summary: Nvidia reports results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's resignation, and Anthropic plans to price its IPO on Wednesday at a valuation of up to $1.45 trillion.[^13][^14] The US says new rules from Nov 19 will limit Chinese access to AI chips through foreign data centres.[^15]

lead.title: Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO lead crucial week for AI bulls

alsoReported.title: Nvidia's first post-Jensen earnings and Anthropic's IPO: What to watch this week
US moves to restrict China's remote access to AI chips after Nvidia row

article: Nvidia, which makes about 90% of the most advanced AI chips, reports quarterly results on Tuesday.[^13] It is its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week amid reports linking him to a person US authorities suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.[^13][^14] Analysts expect revenue of about $109 billion, up roughly 90% from a year earlier.[^13]

On Wednesday, Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude AI models (including the one writing this brief), plans to price its share sale. It is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78, valuing the company at $1.3 to $1.45 trillion, with trading on the Nasdaq from Thursday.[^13][^14] Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, along with a large accounting loss.[^13]

Washington is also changing the rules. The Commerce Department says companies in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil will need US licences for advanced AI chips from Nov 19, to stop Chinese firms renting computing power from data centres abroad.[^15] Business Standard, citing Nikkei Asia, reports that such remote access could make up a quarter of China's AI computing power by the end of 2026.[^15]

Why it matters: AI spending now moves stock markets, pension funds and energy use. Some analysts say strong results could reassure investors; others warn the Huang affair "hasn't hit its bottom yet".[^13][^14] My read: this week will be read as a test of whether investors still trust the AI boom, but one week of numbers will not settle that.
topics.differences: Some strategists see Nvidia's results and Anthropic's listing as possible boosts for AI stocks; a Baird analyst warns of more fallout from the leadership crisis, including possible fines and write-downs.[^13][^14]
